summary: Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned her PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles. In 1998, she became a professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.
Dipa Ma (1911–1989) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw (circa 1964–1967) and Anagarika Munindra (circa 1967–1980). She later taught Sylvia Boorstein.

Dipak Kumar Barua (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Dean of Postgraduate Studies at the University of Calcutta in 1987, was head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1996–2003), and taught Saswati Mutsuddy.

Dipak Ranjan Das is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. He was attested in 1994 at the University of Calcutta's Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture.

Dipesh Chakrabarty (born 1948) is a historian and philosopher. He studied at Presidency University, IIM Calcutta, and the Australian National University (PhD). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1984–1995) and became a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff (born 1938) is a historian and Indologist who earned his MA and doctorate from Leiden University. He served at Leiden as a lecturer (1967) and Chair of Indian History (1971–2003), and founded the EASAS.

Diwakar Acharya (born 1969) is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Ramananda Giri and earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg. He taught at Nepal Sanskrit University and Kyoto University before becoming a professor and fellow at Oxford in 2016.
Dixian (1858–1932) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu from circa 1884 to 1886. He later served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Dmitry Kudryavsky (1867–1920) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at St. Petersburg University from 1886 to 1890. He held an academic post at the Imperial University of Dorpat from circa 1898 to 1918.
Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Dodrupchen Rinpoche (1927–2022) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Kunzang Pelden, and taught Ronald M. Davidson, Tulku Thondup, and Do Trul Tubten Changchub Gyaltsen, among others.

Dominic Goodall is an Indologist who completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and studied with S. A. Srinivasan. He joined the École Française d'Extrême-Orient as a professor in 2000 and lectured at the EPHE in 2005.

Dominic Sur is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under David Germano, Karen Christina Lang, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Khenpo Lama Chönam. He was attested at Utah State University in 2017.

Dominik Wujastyk is an Indologist educated at the University of London and Oxford. His career includes posts at the Wellcome Institute (~1984–2000), UCL (2002–2009), the University of Vienna (2009–2015), and the University of Alberta (2015).

Dominique Sportiche (born 1952) is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (~1977–1984). He joined the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1988 and taught Edward Garrett.

Dominique-Sila Khan (1949–2016) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University. She was attested as a research fellow at the Institute of Rajasthan Studies in 2000.
Don A. Pittman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago. He was attested as a faculty member at Texas Christian University in 2001.

Don Handelman (born 1939) is a scholar of religious studies and anthropology. He studied at McGill University, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Manchester, and served as Professor of Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1972–2007).

Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe (1865–1937) was an Indologist, archaeologist, and linguist who studied under Wilhelm Geiger at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg. He worked as an epigraphist for the Government of Ceylon (~1899–1929) and at the University of London (~1918–1936).

Donald A. Ringe (born 1954) is a linguist and Indologist. He earned an MPhil from Oxford and a PhD from Yale under Warren Cowgill. After teaching Classics at Bard College (1983–1985), he joined the University of Pennsylvania faculty in 1985.
